heard: This Martian canyon stretches from New York to Lowe's Angels. In 1971, the Mariner 9 orbiter discovered this massive scar slashed across the Martian equator. Spanning 4,000 kilometers, it makes the Grand Canyon look like a crack. This system plunges 11 kilometers deep, four times the depth of any gorge on Earth. It didn't form from a slow river, but from the planet literally tearing itself apart three billion years ago. The immense weight of the tharsis volcanic bulge cracked the crust, and colossal landslides widened the jagged gap. Preserved minerals prove that ancient, rushing water once helped carve this giant. These cataclysms are exactly why.
